findings.title: Override is selected for the wrong invitee date when timezone conversion crosses midnight
findings.body: The active-override filter selects a day using the unadjusted `override.start`, but the new code later shifts that override by `inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset` (lines 212-224). That shift can change its invitee calendar date, and only the shifted hour/minute is retained. For example, a 09:00 June 10 override for an Asia/Tokyo organizer is 16:00 June 9 for an America/Los_Angeles attendee: the unshifted timestamp makes this code activate the override for June 10, then the shifted 16:00 minute value produces a June 10 slot instead of June 9. The filter must use the converted instant (and account for range overlap) before deciding which invitee day owns the override.

findings.title: Slots inside an override bypass busy-time validation
findings.body: When a slot is considered inside a date override, `dateOverrideExist` causes this function to return `true` before reaching the `busy.every(...)` check at line 153. `getTimeSlots` creates availability candidates but does not remove calendar or Cal.com booking conflicts, so a host with an override can be offered and booked during an existing busy event. The override should determine whether the host is scheduled to work, then the normal busy-time check must still run.

findings.title: Date-override validation accepts partial overlaps and mishandles multiple override windows
findings.body: The override predicate only rejects slots that are completely before or strictly after one override; it never requires the full `[slotStart, slotEnd]` interval to be contained in an override. A 60-minute slot from 09:30 to 10:30 is therefore accepted for a 10:00 to 11:00 override. In addition, using `find` means a slot in one of several override windows is rejected as soon as another same-day window does not contain it. The intended all-day/zero-length special case at line 114 also cannot work because two separately created Dayjs objects are compared with `===`. This can both expose slots outside a fixed host's override availability and hide valid override slots.

findings.title: Fixed-host normal working hours are not checked as a containing availability range
findings.body: This condition only looks for a working-hours entry that proves the slot invalid; it never requires that any entry for the host actually contains the slot. If a fixed host has no `workingHour` on the slot's weekday, `find` returns undefined and the host falls through as available, allowing a round-robin candidate supplied by a loose host to be booked on the fixed host's day off. Split working-hour ranges are also evaluated incorrectly because a slot valid in one range can be rejected by another, and `end` is set equal to the slot start at line 142 so the event duration is never checked. The check needs to require one host-local working interval containing the complete slot.

findings.title: The added regression test does not cover fixed hosts in a round-robin event
findings.body: The new test invokes an event type with only `users`; it has neither `schedulingType: "ROUND_ROBIN"` nor `hosts` with an `isFixed` host. Consequently it does not exercise the fixed-host filtering path changed in `getSchedule`, and the existing round-robin test also uses `hosts: []`. Add a scenario with a fixed host, a loose round-robin host, and fixed-host date overrides (including unavailable and busy periods) so the behavior described by this PR is actually protected.
